summary.title: Powers of Ideals and the Cohomology of Stalks and Fibers of Morphisms
summary.executive_summary: This paper provides a concise proof refining a theorem by Kodiyalam, Cutkosky, Herzog, and Trung regarding the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of powers of ideals. The author establishes that for a positively graded Noetherian algebra, the limit of the regularity of ideal powers minus a linear term exists and relates to the initial degree of the module. A central contribution is proving a conjecture by Huy Tai Ha, showing this limit equals the maximum of the end degrees of local cohomology of the stalks of a specific projection map. The work further generalizes results by Eisenbud and Harris to cases where the morphism is not finite or flat, comparing the regularity of stalks versus fibers. It introduces geometric criteria involving the dimension of fibers in the closure of the graph of the map to determine when the regularity of saturated powers behaves linearly. The paper also defines invariants for regularity over schemes and establishes conditions under which the maximum regularity of stalks bounds the maximum regularity of fibers, particularly for families of projective schemes close to being flat.

claims.description: The limit of the regularity of powers of ideals exists and is determined by stalk cohomology.
Geometric properties of the morphism determine the asymptotic behavior of regularity.

Executive Summary
This paper provides a concise proof refining a theorem by Kodiyalam, Cutkosky, Herzog, and Trung regarding the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of powers of ideals. The author establishes that for a positively graded Noetherian algebra, the limit of the regularity of ideal powers minus a linear term exists and relates to the initial degree of the module. A central contribution is proving a conjecture by Huy Tai Ha, showing this limit equals the maximum of the end degrees of local cohomology of the stalks of a specific projection map. The work further generalizes results by Eisenbud and Harris to cases where the morphism is not finite or flat, comparing the regularity of stalks versus fibers. It introduces geometric criteria involving the dimension of fibers in the closure of the graph of the map to determine when the regularity of saturated powers behaves linearly. The paper also defines invariants for regularity over schemes and establishes conditions under which the maximum regularity of stalks bounds the maximum regularity of fibers, particularly for families of projective schemes close to being flat.

Research Context
The regularity of powers of ideals is a fundamental topic in commutative algebra. Kodiyalam and Cutkosky, Herzog and Trung proved regularity is eventually linear. Cutkosky provided examples showing erratic behavior of cohomology degrees. Eisenbud and Harris linked regularity to fiber regularity for primary ideals.
